title: Hot-shard throttling leading to embedding/rerank latency and quality drift — analysis & mitigations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2025-02-18 morning, the embeddings + rerank pipeline saw a coordinated degradation: steady throughput loss on a subset of customers and a correlated drop in top-k rerank recall. Symptoms included p99 latency spikes, request queuing on a small set of shard hosts, and model scoring variance for long-prefix queries. This doc captures detection, root cause, mitigations applied, and follow-up work to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-02-18 08:43 UTC — First spike detected by routing alarms: arena-embeddings queue depth > 60% for shard group eu-west-2a
2025-02-18 08:47 UTC — Observability alerted: embedding p99 latency increased from baseline 45ms to 310ms for affected tenants
2025-02-18 08:52 UTC — First customer report: search 95th percentile latencies elevated and occasional timeouts
2025-02-18 09:05 UTC — On-call (Mateo) started live triage, identified hotshard on hosts gpu-emb-27..29. KV cache hitrate for those hosts dropped from 82% to 41%
2025-02-18 09:22 UTC — Emergency mitigation: enabled temporary fallback routing to lower-capacity model variant and expanded autoscale headroom for dedicated pools
2025-02-18 09:40 UTC — Latency improved incrementally; p99 returned to ~70ms for most traffic but quality regressions persisted for long-prefix rerank queries

2025-02-18 10:00 UTC — Root-cause hypothesis formed and validated with trace sampling: a background shard compaction job had coincided with a kernel prewarming regression, producing uneven KV-cache warming and increased GPU GC churn on 3 machines
2025-02-18 13:15 UTC — Permanent mitigations planned and scheduled; rollback/patch PR opened to avoid compaction during business hours and add compaction backoff logic
2025-02-24 — Post-deploy validation run: synthetic long-prefix rerank tests show recall restored to baseline and latency stable under controlled load
detection: The first signal came from our routing/queue-depth alarms for embeddings arena (alert threshold 50%). Secondary signal: Console SLO dashboards showed p99 spikes and a drop in batch sizes for affected hosts. Distributed tracing revealed long waits inside the kernel prewarming step on the three hosts in the hot shard.
impact_summary: Duration: ~1.5 hours of elevated latency and 2.5 hours of degraded quality for a subset of customers. Customer visible effects: 12 tenants experienced >3x p95 latency and ~6 tenants reported decreased rerank recall on long-prefix queries. Unit economics: autoscale burst increased cost for the hour by ~18% for the dedicated pool. No PII exposure or security impact.
root_cause: Combined resource and scheduling interaction: a scheduled shard compaction job ran concurrently with a kernel prewarming update (runtime-1.19 candidate) on a small set of GPUs. The compaction temporarily increased memory pressure and evicted hot KV entries; the prewarming regression caused repeated kernel re-initializations under load. Together these caused persistent KV cache misses, smaller effective batching, and queuing on the affected shard hosts. The cluster autoscaler was conservative for these hosts due to recent capacity tuning, delaying replacement, which amplified the outage window.
mitigations_applied: Immediate — route ~30% of traffic off affected shard group to compatible model variants (fallback routing) to relieve queuing
Immediate — increased dedicated pool autoscale headroom for eu-west-2a and temporarily allowed faster scale-up for affected instance types
Short-term — paused scheduled compaction jobs during peak hours across all embedding clusters
Short-term — rolled back the kernel prewarming change from runtime-1.19 candidate on the affected hosts
Monitoring — added KV-cache heatmap tracing to identify hot/warm key churn per-shard
permanent_fixes: 1) Scheduler: implement compaction backoff with awareness of request load and KV-cache heatmaps
2) Runtime: fix prewarming regression and add unit+integration tests that reproduce prewarm under synthetic heavy-concurrency workloads
3) Autoscaler: relax the conservative scale-up cooldown for high-priority shard groups and add a fast-path for emergency replacement
4) Routing: add probabilistic multi-shard routing to avoid single hot-shard dependencies for high-traffic tenant slices
5) Observability: expose per-tenant/deployment KV-cache hitrate and per-host kernel reset counters in Console
validation: Post-patch canary run (runtime-1.19.1) across 10% of traffic for two days. Synthetic regression harness for long-prefix rerank datasets passed with recall within +/-0.7% of baseline and p99 latency within +8ms under 90th-percentile traffic profiles. No new KV cache thrash observed in heatmaps.

notes: This incident highlights an important cross-cutting risk: background maintenance (compaction) can interact with runtime-level behavior (kernel prewarm) to produce emergent failures. Team-level ownerships should coordinate scheduling windows and have automated safety gates. The solution path here combines runtime hardening, smarter compaction scheduling, and routing resilience to reduce blast radius.

resolution: Immediate mitigations routed traffic away and rolled back the prewarm change. Permanent fixes implemented across runtime and scheduling; follow-up Linear tickets created and tracked. Post-deploy validation confirms metrics returned to baseline and synthetic rerank quality restored.
retrospective: Action: increase cross-team coordination prior to rollout of background maintenance or runtime changes; require a simulated compaction + prewarm test in CI for any future kernel or compaction-related change. Update runbooks and add automatic circuit-breaker for compaction when per-host request latency exceeds threshold.
